newsitem.title: USA: Court issues asset freeze in Duracell case.
newsitem.headline: Court issues asset freeze in Duracell case.

text.p: A Manhattan federal court has issued a freeze order on profits allegedly made by unknown defendants charged with insider trading on Duracell International Inc securities before Duracell's merger with Gillette Co was announced on September 12, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.

Paul Gerlach, SEC associate director, enforcement division, said the court also granted expedited discovery and has set a preliminary hearing on the agency's motion for a preliminary injunction for September 26.
In a civil complaint filed on Monday, the SEC charged that the defendants hauled in $950,000 when they bought Duracell stock options just days before the merger announcement was made.

The trades were made through accounts maintained by the Lugano, Switzerland,-based BSI-Banca de la Svizzera through Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp and by Nominees (Bahamas) Ltd, a trust holding company in the Bahamas, at Prudential Securities Inc, court papers showed.
The two institutions have thus far refused to disclose the names of their clients.
